hints: Focus on comparing moles, not just grams, since the product has a different Mr from the starting alcohol.
Notice that 74.00 g of each C4 alcohol is exactly 1 mol, so the theoretical product mass is simply the Mr of the ketone or carboxylic acid.
Divide each actual mass by its theoretical mass and multiply by 100 to check if you really get 62% in all three cases.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of starting alcohol**

All three starting alcohols are isomers of formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Their Mr is 74.0.

$$M_r = (4 \times 12.0) + (10 \times 1.0) + 16.0 = 74.0$$

So 74.00 g is 1.00 mol in every case:
$$n = \frac{74.00}{74.0} = 1.00 \text{ mol}$$

**Find theoretical mass of each product**

The mole ratio alcohol : product is 1 : 1 for oxidation.

For 1, butanone $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$ has Mr = 72.0, so theoretical mass = 72.0 g.

For 2 and 3, butanoic acid and 2-methylpropanoic acid $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ have Mr = 88.0, so theoretical mass = 88.0 g.

**Check percentage yield**

Use the yield rule:
$$\% \text{ yield} = \frac{\text{actual mass}}{\text{theoretical mass}} \times 100$$

For 1: $44.64 / 72.0 \times 100 = 62\%$. This matches.

For 2 and 3: $54.56 / 88.0 \times 100 = 62\%$. This also matches.

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all consistent with a 62% yield, the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three statements give 62% yield. Statement 1 gives 44.64/72.0 = 0.62 and statements 2 and 3 give 54.56/88.0 = 0.62.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes only 1 and 2. Statement 3 is also valid because 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropanoic acid have the same Mrs as in statement 2, so it also gives 62% yield and should not be left out.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes only 2 and 3. Statement 1 is also valid because 44.64 g out of a theoretical 72.0 g of butanone is exactly 62% and should not be left out.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination includes only 1. Statements 2 and 3 are also valid oxidations of primary alcohols to carboxylic acids with the same 62% yield, so limiting to 1 alone is incomplete.
